
# Enviromentypes

# 0. Libraries
library(sf)

## Landcover percentage
**Sample Points**
```{r load-sample-points}
sample_points <- read.csv(
  "C:/Users/Lukas/Documents/GitHub/btp_metagenomics/sample_points.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
points_sf   <- st_as_sf(sample_points,
                        coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
                        crs    = 4326)
points_proj <- st_transform(points_sf, 28355)
```

**Virtual-mosaic of Tifs**
```{r build-virtual-mosaic, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# 2. Build an in-R mosaic of all your Landcover tiles and reproject
tile_files <- list.files(
  "C:/Users/Lukas/Documents/GitHub/btp_metagenomics/Landcover/Tif",
  pattern    = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
rasters    <- lapply(tile_files, terra::rast)
mosaic_all <- do.call(mosaic, c(rasters, list(fun = "first")))
landcover_proj <- project(mosaic_all, "EPSG:28355")
```

**Generate Bufferzones**
```{r extract-buffer}
# 3 Buffer zones & exact extraction
buffers   <- st_buffer(points_proj, dist = 150)
extracted <- exact_extract(landcover_proj, buffers)

summary_list <- lapply(seq_along(extracted), function(i) {
  df  <- extracted[[i]]
  agg <- aggregate(df$coverage_fraction,
                   by   = list(class = round(df$value)),
                   FUN  = sum)
  colnames(agg) <- c("land_cover_class", "fraction")
  agg$percent <- round(100 * agg$fraction / sum(agg$fraction), 2)
  agg$id      <- sample_points$id[i]
  agg
})
result_df <- bind_rows(summary_list)
```

```{r climate variable data}

# 5a. Grab the Australia bioclim variables (returns a SpatRaster)
wc_aus <- worldclim_country(
  country = "AUS",    # ISO code
  var     = "bio",    # all 19 BIO variables
  res     = 0.5,      # 30″ resolution
  path    = "data/aus"
)

# 5b. Rename the layers to "bio1"…"bio19" so we can index 1–12
orig <- names(wc_aus)
new  <- sub(".*bio[_~\\.](\\d+)$", "bio\\1", orig)
names(wc_aus) <- new

# 5c. Reproject your 150 m buffers into geographic coords (lon/lat)
buffers_ll <- st_transform(buffers, st_crs(wc_aus))

# 5d. Extract weighted means for bio1…bio12 and give them proper names ----

# a) Define the codes and descriptive names
bio_codes <- paste0("bio", 1:12)
bio_names <- c(
  annual_mean_temp           = "bio1",
  mean_diurnal_range         = "bio2",
  isothermality              = "bio3",
  temp_seasonality           = "bio4",
  max_temp_warmest_month     = "bio5",
  min_temp_coldest_month     = "bio6",
  temp_annual_range          = "bio7",
  mean_temp_wettest_quarter  = "bio8",
  mean_temp_driest_quarter   = "bio9",
  mean_temp_warmest_quarter  = "bio10",
  mean_temp_coldest_quarter  = "bio11",
  annual_precipitation       = "bio12"
)

# b) Pull out each layer’s weighted mean into a list
means_list <- purrr::map(bio_codes, function(code) {
  exactextractr::exact_extract(
    wc_aus[[code]],
    buffers_ll,
    fun = function(vals, coverage_fraction) {
      weighted.mean(vals, coverage_fraction, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  )
})

# c) Build a tibble: sample IDs + one column per bio
clim_df <- tibble::tibble(id = sample_points$id) %>%
  dplyr::bind_cols(as_tibble(purrr::set_names(means_list, bio_codes))) %>%
  # d) Rename from bio# → descriptive
  dplyr::rename(!!!bio_names)

print(clim_df)

```

```{r population variable data, eva}
# 1. Download & load the 1 km WorldPop density for Australia -------------
out1km <- "data/pop1km/aus_pd_2020_1km.tif"
dir.create(dirname(out1km), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

download.file(
  "https://data.worldpop.org/GIS/Population_Density/Global_2000_2020_1km/2020/AUS/aus_pd_2020_1km.tif",
  out1km, mode = "wb"
)
pop1km_rast <- rast(out1km)

# 2. Reproject your 150 m buffers into the raster’s CRS (WGS84 lon/lat)
buffers_ll <- st_transform(buffers, st_crs(pop1km_rast))

# 3. For each buffer, compute the mean density (people / km²)
pop1km_mean <- exact_extract(pop1km_rast, buffers_ll, fun = "mean")

# 4. Assemble into a data‐frame
pop1km_df <- tibble(
  id              = sample_points$id,
  pop_density_1km = pop1km_mean
)

print(pop1km_df)
```

```{r landcover_plot_fixed, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# 1. Read style file and extract labels
qml_path <- "C:/Users/Lukas/Documents/GitHub/btp_metagenomics/Landcover/landcover_class_cyear_4_style.qml"
stopifnot(file.exists(qml_path))

qml_raw <- read_xml(qml_path)
qml      <- xml_ns_strip(qml_raw)

# 2) Grab every <paletteEntry> (that’s where your value/label/color live)
entries <- xml_find_all(qml, ".//paletteEntry")

style_df <- tibble(
  land_cover_class       = as.integer(xml_attr(entries, "value")),
  land_cover_description = xml_attr(entries, "label"),
  color                  = xml_attr(entries, "color")
)

# 2. Join descriptions onto your result_df
result_df <- result_df %>%
  left_join(
    style_df %>% select(land_cover_class, land_cover_description),
    by = "land_cover_class"
  )


# 7. Plot stacked bar of your continuous group totals
# define your group colours
group_colors <- c(
  "Cultivated Vegetation - Woody"      = "#6a51a3",
  "Cultivated Vegetation - Herbaceous" = "#9e9ac8",
  "Natural Vegetation - Woody"         = "#006400",
  "Natural Vegetation - Herbaceous"    = "#1b9e77",
  "Natural Vegetation - General"       = "#b2df8a",
  "Natural Vegetation - Sparse"        = "#e6c229",
  "Aquatic Vegetation"                 = "#41b6c4",
  "Bare Surface"                       = "#e6ab02",
  "Urban/Artificial"                   = "#757575",
  "Water"                              = "#1f78b4",
  "Other"                              = "#cccccc"
)

summary_df <- result_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(land_cover_description)) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    Cultivated_Total   = sum(percent[grepl("^Cultivated", land_cover_description)], na.rm=TRUE),
    Native_Total       = sum(percent[grepl("^Natural Terrestrial", land_cover_description)], na.rm=TRUE),
    Aquatic_Vegetation = sum(percent[grepl("Aquatic", land_cover_description)], na.rm=TRUE),
    Water              = sum(percent[grepl("^Water", land_cover_description)], na.rm=TRUE),
    Artificial_Bare    = sum(percent[grepl("Surface", land_cover_description)], na.rm=TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2) Pivot to long for plotting
plot_df <- summary_df %>%
  pivot_longer(-id, names_to="group", values_to="pct") %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = names(group_colors)))

# 3) Plot exactly as before
p <- ggplot(summary_df, aes(x = factor(id), y = pct, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors, na.value = "gray90") +
  labs(
    title = "Landcover Continuous Groups per Sample",
    x     = "Sample ID",
    y     = "Percent Cover",
    fill  = "Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
    legend.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

print(p)
ggsave("landcover_continuous_groups.png", p, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

```{r landcover_proportion matrix}
landcover_prop <- landcover_wide %>%
  mutate(across(-id, ~ . / 100))
# Remove id column for calculations
prop_matrix <- landcover_prop %>% select(-id) %>% as.matrix()
```

```{r landcover_diversity}
# Calculate indices for each sample (row)
shannon <- diversity(prop_matrix, index = "shannon")
simpson <- diversity(prop_matrix, index = "simpson")
richness <- specnumber(prop_matrix)

# Hill numbers: effective number of landcover types
hill_q0 <- richness                    # q = 0 (species richness)
hill_q1 <- exp(shannon)                # q = 1 (exponential Shannon)
hill_q2 <- 1 / (1 - simpson)           # q = 2 (inverse Simpson). 


# Combine with original data
landcover_wide <- landcover_wide %>%
  mutate(
    shannon = shannon,
    simpson = simpson,
    hill_q0 = hill_q0,
    hill_q1 = hill_q1,
    hill_q2 = hill_q2
  )
```

**hill visualisation**
```{r hill_visualisation}

hill_long <- landcover_wide %>%
  select(id, hill_q0, hill_q1, hill_q2) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("hill_q"),
               names_to = "q",
               values_to = "value")

save(hill_long, 
     file = "data/hill.Rdata")

ggplot(hill_long, aes(x = q, y = value, group = id, color = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Hill Numbers per Sample (Landcover Types)",
    x = "Hill Order (q)",
    y = "Effective Diversity (# Landcover Types)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r dominante_landcover}
# Pivot to long for easier processing
landcover_long <- continuous_df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -id,
    names_to = "landcover_type",
    values_to = "percent_cover"
  )

# Find the dominant (highest percent_cover) per sample
dominant_by_sample <- landcover_long %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  filter(percent_cover == max(percent_cover, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%     # In case of ties
  ungroup() %>%
  select(id, dominant_landcover = landcover_type, dom_percent_cover = percent_cover)

# Merge with your diversity measures
continuous_df <- continuous_df %>%
  left_join(dominant_by_sample, by = "id")
```

```{r dominant_boxplot}

ggplot(continuous_df, aes(x=dominant_landcover, y=shannon, fill=dominant_landcover)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha=.8, outlier.color="red", outlier.size=1.5) +
  theme_minimal(base_size=14) +
  labs(
    title = "Diversity (Shannon) by Dominant Landcover Type",
    x = "Dominant Landcover",
    y = "Shannon Diversity Index"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, vjust=1),
        legend.position = "none")
```

```{r dominant_summary}
dominant_summary <- continuous_df %>%
  count(dominant_landcover, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(perc = 100 * n / sum(n))

print(dominant_summary)
```

```{r merge-with-metadata, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# 8. Merge totals & groups into metadata

NaturalvsCultivated <- left_join(sample_metadata, landcover_wide, by = c("sample" = "id"))
```

**scatter-plot**
```{r scatter-plots-basic, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# use the new summary totals: cultivated_total, natural_total, urban_total
plots_df <- NaturalvsCultivated %>%
  rename(
    Cultivated = Cultivated_Total,
    Natural    = Native_Total,
    Urban      = Artificial_Bare
  )

# Cultivated vs diversity
p_cult <- ggplot(plots_df, aes(x = Cultivated, y = diversity)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(
    title = "Microbiome Diversity vs. Cultivated Cover",
    x = "Cultivated Cover (%)",
    y = "Diversity"
  )
# Natural vs diversity
p_nat <- ggplot(plots_df, aes(x = Natural, y = diversity)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(
    title = "Microbiome Diversity vs. Natural Cover",
    x = "Natural Cover (%)",
    y = "Diversity"
  )
# Urban vs diversity
p_urb <- ggplot(plots_df, aes(x = Urban, y = diversity)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(
    title = "Microbiome Diversity vs. Urban/Bare Cover",
    x = "Urban/Bare Cover (%)",
    y = "Diversity"
  )

# print all three
print(p_cult)
print(p_nat)
print(p_urb)
```

**linear-model**
```{r linear-model-and-boxplot, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
lm_mod <- lm(
  diversity ~ Cultivated_Total + Native_Total + Artificial_Bare,
  data = NaturalvsCultivated
)
print(summary(lm_mod))


# boxplot by a categorical environmental variable, e.g. "broad_environment"
ggplot(NaturalvsCultivated, aes(x = broad_environment, y = diversity)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Diversity by Broad Environment", x = "Broad Environment", y = "Diversity")
```

**boxplot**
```{r categorize-native-cultivated, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# 11. Categorise continuous covers into Low/Med/High & boxplots

NaturalvsCultivated <- NaturalvsCultivated %>%
  mutate(
    native_group = cut(
      Native_Total,
      breaks = c(-1, 25, 75, 100),
      labels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")
    ),
    cultivated_group = cut(
      Cultivated_Total,
      breaks = c(-1, 25, 75, 100),
      labels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")
    )
  )

# Boxplot: diversity ~ native_group
ggplot(NaturalvsCultivated, aes(x = native_group, y = diversity)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#1b9e77") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Diversity by Native Vegetation Group",
    x     = "Native Cover Group",
    y     = "Diversity"
  )

# Boxplot: diversity ~ cultivated_group
ggplot(NaturalvsCultivated, aes(x = cultivated_group, y = diversity)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#6a51a3") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Diversity by Cultivated Vegetation Group",
    x     = "Cultivated Cover Group",
    y     = "Diversity"
  )

```
